record.paper_title: A single impurity in an ideal atomic Fermi gas: current understanding and some open problems
record.original_question: For composite dressed quasiparticles in this impurity problem, including the dimeron, trimeron, and tetrameron, determine whether there is a stronger general lower bound on the effective mass than positivity alone, namely whether dressing always increases the mass so that M*_b / M_b >= 1, where M_b is the bare mass of the corresponding composite bound state and M*_b is its effective mass in the Fermi gas.

evidence.quote: Is there a better bound for dimerons, trimerons and tetramerons?
We conjecture that the dressing always increases the mass, even for composite particles: M∗ b /Mb ≥ 1?
All calculations of the effective mass of the dimeron so far are consistent with this simple generalisation [5, 20].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a single distinguishable impurity of bare mass $M_{\rm imp}$ immersed in a non-interacting (ideal) gas of identical fermions of mass $m$ at zero temperature in three dimensions. The impurity interacts with the fermions through a short-range two-body interaction characterized by the s-wave scattering length $a$. Depending on $a$ and on the mass ratio $M_{\rm imp}/m$, the impurity together with $b\ge 1$ fermions can form a bound cluster in vacuum (a $b$-mer): $b=1$ gives the bare impurity (polaron sector), $b=2$ the dimer (dimeron sector), $b=3$ the trimer (trimeron sector), $b=4$ the tetramer (tetrameron sector). Let $M_b = M_{\rm imp} + b\,m$ denote the bare total mass of such a $b$-cluster.

When this cluster is placed in the Fermi sea, it becomes a dressed quasiparticle (polaron, dimeron, trimeron, tetrameron, ...) with a well-defined dispersion $E_b(\mathbf{P})$ near zero total momentum $\mathbf{P}=0$. The effective mass $M_b^*$ is defined by
$$E_b(\mathbf{P}) = E_b(0) + \frac{|\mathbf{P}|^2}{2 M_b^*} + o(|\mathbf{P}|^2), \qquad |\mathbf{P}|\to 0.$$

Question. Prove or disprove the following conjecture: for every such composite dressed quasiparticle (in particular for the dimeron, trimeron, and tetrameron) in a polarized ideal Fermi gas, dressing by the medium can only increase the inertia, i.e.
$$\frac{M_b^*}{M_b} \;\ge\; 1.$$
Equivalently, find a general lower bound on $M_b^*/M_b$ that is strictly stronger than the trivial positivity bound $M_b^* > 0$, valid throughout the parameter range (mass ratio and scattering length) in which the corresponding composite bound state exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that dressing increases the mass of composite quasiparticles (dimerons, trimerons, tetramerons) in a polarized ideal Fermi gas, i.e. $M^*_b/M_b\ge 1$, appears to remain an open problem. Existing literature on Fermi polarons and dimerons reports calculations consistent with the bound, and rigorous lower bounds on effective masses have been established only for related (Fröhlich-type) polaron models, not for these composite few-body dressed states. No proof or counterexample for the stated composite-mass bound was located.

status_evidence.title: A single impurity in an ideal atomic Fermi gas (arXiv:1404.3220)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the conjecture M*_b/M_b >= 1 for composite quasiparticles (dimeron, trimeron, tetrameron) as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The composite effective-mass bound is posed as an open conjecture in the impurity literature.

status_evidence.title: Effective Mass of the Polaron: A Lower Bound (Comm. Math. Phys., 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous lower bounds on the effective mass have been derived for the Fröhlich polaron, a different model.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous mass bounds exist for related polaron models but not for the composite Fermi-gas quasiparticles in question.

status_evidence.title: Effective mass of the Fröhlich Polaron and the Landau–Pekar–Spohn conjecture (arXiv:2307.13058)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on effective-mass conjectures concerns Fröhlich polarons, with no extension to dimerons/trimerons.
status_evidence.claim: No general result establishing M*_b/M_b >= 1 for composite Fermi-gas quasiparticles is reported.
